name: Fairfax VA, USA (Base)

rent.notes: Virginia has no rental tax. Water, sewage, and trash are separate utility bills (not included in rent).

groceries.notes: NOVA grocery prices 15-20% above national average

electricity.notes: Dominion Energy. Avg across seasons — $100 winter, $220 summer A/C. Includes general household.

gas.notes: Washington Gas. Natural gas heating (Nov–Mar primary), cooking, water heater.

sewage.notes: Billed with water. Fairfax County sanitary sewer charge.

trash.notes: Fairfax County solid waste. Billed quarterly (~$90/qtr).

utilities.taxes: Virginia exempts residential utilities from state sales tax.
utilities.notes: Dominion bill is about $180/mo at 1,000 kWh (Oct 2026), and sewer FY2027 is $55.78/qtr base plus $9.88 per 1,000 gal, about $58/mo at 12k gal/qtr. Fairfax Water averages about $26/mo, derived from a $1.93 rise equal to 7.5%. Range assumes 800-1,400 kWh. Trash/RUBS fees and any gas are estimates, not sourced.

sources.title: Fairfax residents utility bills set to rise in 2026 (Fairfax Times)
Fairfax Water proposes annual rate increase

healthcare.notes: Uses the 2026 Part B standard premium of $202.90 x2, since 2027 is not yet published. Medigap G at age 65 in Virginia runs $138 (cheapest) to $156 among listed carriers, with a $236 average (MoneyGeek, 2026). Part D runs $0 to the $38.99 base beneficiary premium per person. This is not Fairfax-specific, and attained-age Plan G rises with age.

sources.title: Medigap Plan G premiums rose 12 to 26 percent in 2026 filings (247WallSt)
Medicare Part D plan premiums 2026 (Healthcare Dive)

healthcarePreMedicare.notes: KFF 2027 Virginia statewide averages for a 40-year-old are bronze $403, benchmark silver $549 and lowest gold $518, scaled to age 60 with the federal default age curve (2.714/1.278) for two people. Lowest gold ($2,200 for two) is below benchmark silver because of silver loading, so max is set to the benchmark. These are statewide averages, not Fairfax-specific.

sources.title: KFF Average Monthly Marketplace Premiums by Metal Tier

insurance.notes: Fairfax renters quotes average about $8/mo (range $6-18). Insure.com lists Fairfax ZIP 22035 at $20/mo and the Virginia average at $22/mo for $40k property and $300k liability. Higher liability limits for a large dog could push costs above this range.

sources.title: Average renters insurance cost in Virginia (Insure.com)

petCare.notes: Vet care in NOVA premium-priced. VCA, Pender, and Fairfax Animal Hospital nearby.

petDaycare.notes: Rover Fairfax daycare averages $39/day (range $29-45), and Dogtopia Fairfax City charges $41/day on an 8-day pass or $43/day on a 4-day pass, with $75/night boarding for non-enrolled dogs. Min is 8 days at $39, typical is an 8-day pass plus 1 boarding night, and max is 12 days at $43.

petGrooming.notes: Dogtopia Fairfax charges $50 for a large-dog bath, plus $15 nails, $15 ear or teeth care and brush-outs from $15, which puts a monthly bath at about $80. Fairfax full-deshed prices for a Bernese were not published, so typical and max are the stored values.

transportation.notes: Inputs: Virginia gas at $4.14/gal (AAA, Sep 2026) over 600-1,000 mi/mo at 25 mpg, and full coverage at age 65 of $92-194/mo (state average $1,709/yr). Fairfax car tax is $4.57 per $100, net of PPTRA relief. Maintenance and the registration fee are estimates, not sourced.

sources.title: Gas prices jump in Richmond, across Virginia (12 On Your Side)
Cheap car insurance for seniors in Virginia (CarInsurance.com)
Fairfax County vehicle personal property tax

entertainment.notes: Fios 1 Gig is $89.99/mo with AutoPay. BLS puts Washington-metro food away from home at $5,905/yr per household (about $492/mo), which supports the stored dining and activities assumptions. Streaming and activities line items are not separately sourced.

clothing.notes: BLS puts Washington-metro apparel at 3.3% of $108,215/yr, about $298/mo for a 2.4-person working household, which is used as max. A retired couple is assumed to spend less, so min and typical are judgment calls under that ceiling.

personalCare.notes: BLS puts Washington-metro personal care at 1.5% of $108,215/yr, about $135/mo per household, which is used as max. Min and typical are scaled down for a retired couple and are judgment calls.

phoneCell.notes: US Mobile Unlimited Starter is $50 for 2 lines with taxes included, and Visible is $25/line. T-Mobile Essentials Saver is $80 for 2 lines plus taxes, and Verizon starts at $110 (all prices Oct 2026).

sources.title: Best cell phone plans for 2 lines October 2026 (US Mobile)

miscellaneous.notes: HOA contributions, parking permits, EZ-Pass tolls common in NOVA

buffer.notes: Monthly safety buffer for unexpected expenses

medicalOOP.notes: Anti-VEGF injections for macular degeneration (~$300-400 OOP each, 6-10x/yr after Medicare 80%). Specialist visits: ophthalmologist q6-8wks, endocrinologist 2-4x/yr, cardiologist 1-2x/yr. Frequent labs: lipid panel, TSH, A1C, CMP 3-4x/yr each. Both adults: PCP visits quarterly.

medicine.notes: Monthly prescription medication costs for household

taxes.notes: Estimated monthly income tax on $72,000/yr household income. Based on jurisdiction's effective retiree rate; excludes sales/VAT/property tax.

stateIncomeTax.exemptions: Age 65+ deduction $12K/person. SS fully exempt from VA tax.

salesTax.notes: Fairfax County 6% (4.3% state + 0.7% regional + 1% NOVA transit)

propertyTax.notes: Renters: no direct property tax. Vehicle personal property ~$4.57/$100 assessed.

healthcare.notes: Inova Fairfax Medical Center (Level I trauma), Virginia Hospital Center, access to Johns Hopkins/Georgetown specialists. Excellent healthcare infrastructure.

acaMarketplace.notes: NOVA marketplace: Anthem HealthKeepers, CareFirst, Kaiser. Metro pricing.
acaMarketplace.disclaimer: Estimated ±15% vs healthcare.gov quote — verify for a specific ZIP before relying on the number.

lifestyle.notes: Burke Lake Park, Lake Accotink, numerous dog parks. Diverse dining scene. Close to DC cultural amenities.

sources.title: Virginia DOT — Social Security and Tier 1 Railroad Retirement subtractions

pros: Proximity to DC cultural resources (Smithsonian, etc.)

cons.text: Safety & crime: see cited reports for current figures by city and country
